lesson_title: One Law, Every Solid: Prisms and Cylinders
hook_text: The wrapper on a tin is secretly a rectangle — and it hands you the whole formula.
clip_script: The tin unfolds into three pieces, and the middle piece is the revelation. Top and bottom are circles: pi r squared each, sixteen pi apiece, thirty-two pi together. The curved wall, cut down its seam and laid flat, is a rectangle. Its height is the tin's height, fifteen. Its width is the distance once around the rim — the circumference, two pi r, which is eight pi. The curved surface is therefore two pi r times h: eight pi times fifteen, one hundred and twenty pi. Grand total: thirty-two pi plus one hundred and twenty pi — one hundred and fifty-two pi square centimetres exactly, which rounds to 477,52.
visual_style: A paint tin spinning, its wrapper peeling away and flattening into a glowing rectangle, the circumference unrolling along a ruler, formulas assembling themselves from the pieces.
pacing: Slow peel for the reveal, brisk assembly of the three areas, clean landing on 152 pi.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and make every prism and cylinder answer to one law.
